Read only source /evidence/source.json, parent /evidence/parent.json, and independent audit /evidence/audit.json. Do not use the web, any prior-run file other than those exact sealed inputs, any other solution, or any verification report. You may create exact-arithmetic checks only under /work; do not modify files outside /work.

Parent SHA-256: 508aa9f77a685486000c0b4f9c59054371d98c734d4e542c026043683a951220
Audit SHA-256: 743094b5220c24b94194b3c8b782f9487a90412d1cfa7a97951cd9a609095004

This is an exact-closure attempt after the three scheduled search lenses. Concentrate on resolving the independent audit. If no material proof change is required, copy claimed_resolution, every claim and proof_sketch, and final_writeup from the parent exactly.

Address every REFUTED or UNRESOLVED claim and the audit's target-coverage judgment. Preserve correct progress. Repair, narrow, replace, or remove unsupported claims. Never call the open target solved without a complete proof at the requested strength. Put every load-bearing claim in a separate results item in proof order. There is no claim-count cap. The entire ordered proof is in scope. Keep final_writeup under 3,000 words and each proof_sketch under 500 words.

  "record_id": "tcs_incremental_toposort_nsqrtm",
  "stage": "REVISION_AUDIT",
  "arm": "plain",

  "parent_sha256": "508aa9f77a685486000c0b4f9c59054371d98c734d4e542c026043683a951220",

  "claims": [
    {
      "idx": 0,
      "claim": "The two source-stated bounds imply total update time Õ(min{n²,m^(4/3)}). This meets Õ(n√m) when m≤n^(6/5) and when m≥n²/log^{O(1)}n; over all m it is within an Õ(n^(1/4)) factor of the target.",
      "claim_sha256": "79003b417cee6573b8c836f7fd4f5efe82f393a8dfcd3dfee6043f7ded223a27",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "For the sparse bound, m^(4/3)≤n√m is equivalent to m^(5/6)≤n, hence m≤n^(6/5). For the dense bound, n²/(n√m)=n/√m is polylogarithmic when m≥n²/polylog(n). The ratio min{n²,m^(4/3)}/(n√m)=min{n/√m,m^(5/6)/n}; its increasing and decreasing branches meet at m=n^(3/2), where the ratio is n^(1/4).",
      "witness": "The crossover m=n^(3/2) makes both available bounds n² and realizes the claimed worst-case n^(1/4) ratio.",
      "search_method": "Symbolic exponent comparison followed by exact-integer inequality checks.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_incremental_toposort_nsqrtm/audit/plain/attempt_6/audit_attempt6_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 1,
      "claim": "Balanced-cut lemma: for every order-violating insertion u→v into a DAG, either the insertion closes a cycle, or one can find equally sized sets B,F and a cut c such that F consists of the descendants of v at or left of c, B consists of the ancestors of u right of c, and the stable order (L\\F),B,F,(R\\B) is topological. In the latter case, all |B||F| ordered pairs in B×F become newly reachable.",
      "claim_sha256": "1a373761ae60fc74a6b3d22660333f85a2d6067791f2f307eda805a6ac373c39",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "If v reaches u, u→v closes a cycle. Otherwise the inclusive descendant and ancestor sets D,C inside [v,u] are disjoint. During a cut sweep, |D∩L|−|C∩R| starts negative, ends positive, and changes only by unit positive steps, so it attains zero with v∈F and u∈B. The only newly reversed old-edge categories are F→L\\F, R\\B→B, and F→B; these contradict descendant closure, ancestor closure, and absence of a v-to-u path, respectively. The new edge points B→F. Every b∈B reaches every f∈F through b→u→v→f, while the old topological order placed f before b, proving every such pair is fresh.",
      "witness": "The zero of the integer cut-sweep supplies the required B,F,c constructively.",
      "search_method": "Direct invariant proof plus exhaustive enumeration of all fixed-order DAGs through six vertices and every candidate violating insertion.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_incremental_toposort_nsqrtm/audit/plain/attempt_6/audit_attempt6_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 2,
      "claim": "The balanced-cut construction gives an explicit combinatorial algorithm with total time Õ(m+n√m+A), where A is the total number of adjacency entries scanned from selected forward vertices and selected backward vertices. Consequently it attains Õ(n√m) whenever A=Õ(n√m), including sequences in which every selected forward vertex has polylogarithmic out-degree and every selected backward vertex has polylogarithmic in-degree at its expansion time.",
      "claim_sha256": "1e3b755a91cfb2c9e7b71b948548bc049c5686be8c3f70aea12a6364f7205a45",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "For each acyclic violating update, q² ordered pairs become newly reachable. Monotonicity makes these charged pairs disjoint across updates, so Σq_i²≤n(n−1); Cauchy–Schwarz gives Σq_i=O(n√m). Heap operations generated by scanned edges cost Õ(A), selected-vertex and stable-order operations cost Õ(Σq_i), and input/root work costs Õ(m); the sole terminal cycle search adds at most Õ(n)+its A contribution. Thus the stated total follows. Under the directional polylog-degree condition, A=Õ(Σq_i+n), and for a simple graph m≤n² implies m≤n√m.",
      "witness": "The accounting identity Σq_i≤√(mΣq_i²)≤n√m is supported by the fresh-pair invariant from claim 1.",
      "search_method": "Independent amortized-analysis reconstruction; exhaustive tests also confirmed that the paired compatible search returns balanced fresh-pair sets.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_incremental_toposort_nsqrtm/audit/plain/attempt_6/audit_attempt6_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 3,
      "claim": "Full adjacency-list rescanning cannot be charged automatically to the balanced-search vertex bound: there is a DAG sequence with n=2r+2 and m=4r in which every violating update has q=1 and creates exactly one new reachability pair, yet rescanning the selected forward list costs r².",
      "claim_sha256": "52567c84ad8041cb3bc36f8d47aa749b024b2b3014b8efa9e2e527fc45212061",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "With order v,u₁,…,u_r,z,w₁,…,w_r, the 3r initial edges v→w_j, z→w_j, and u_i→z are consistent. Before inserting u_i→v, the relevant descendant and ancestor sets are {v} and {u_i}, so q=1. Vertex u_i already reaches z and every w_j and has no proper ancestor, hence only (u_i,v) is newly reachable. Vertex v nevertheless has r outgoing entries on each of r violating updates, producing exactly r² full-list scans. Counts are n=2r+2 and m=4r.",
      "witness": "The construction works for every integer r≥1; the checker reconstructs every update and its exact reachability delta for 1≤r≤40.",
      "search_method": "Exact construction simulation with integer reachability closure and stable reorder checks.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_incremental_toposort_nsqrtm/audit/plain/attempt_6/audit_attempt6_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 4,
      "claim": "Interval-pruning lemma: in a compatible-search round whose current forward-minimum and backward-maximum candidates are f≺b, forward expansion may ignore out-neighbors right of b and backward expansion may ignore in-neighbors left of f. The pruned search still detects every cycle-forming insertion and, in the non-cycle branch, selects the same first q descendants and last q ancestors that yield a balanced cut.",
      "claim_sha256": "af6ddd6067c56bee1ecfe58ebb99c4efd05fc0f150ba09db2f21bf11fec868a5",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Forward extracted candidates are monotone rightward and backward extracted candidates monotone leftward. Thus a forward neighbor discarded to the right of the current b can never participate in a later compatible pair; its descendants lie still farther right. The backward argument is symmetric, proving preservation of the non-cycle selections. For a cycle path v=p₀→⋯→p_k=u, if expansion of p_i first discards p_(i+1)>b, then every suffix vertex is right of b. Backward expansion from u has already propagated down that suffix: at each earlier expansion its predecessor lay right of the then-current forward frontier and was not pruned. Consequently p_i belongs to both reached sets, forcing cycle detection.",
      "witness": "Full and pruned searches produced identical non-cycle selections and identical cycle decisions for all 251,085 tested insertions through n=6.",
      "search_method": "Monotone-frontier/path-induction proof plus exhaustive comparison against unpruned compatible search.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_incremental_toposort_nsqrtm/audit/plain/attempt_6/audit_attempt6_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 5,
      "claim": "Selective-expansion refinement: let H sum, over all compatible-search expansions, min{outdeg(f),|{x:f≺x≼b}|} on the forward side and min{indeg(b),|{x:f≼x≺b}|} on the backward side. There is an explicit combinatorial implementation with total update time Õ(m+n√m+H). Moreover H≤A, and H=O(m) on the rescanning family of the preceding audited claim.",
      "claim_sha256": "9b913a4b3f8715e6ab51ad9a810122eee20099bdb4f93fdcce2938290720122f",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "The algorithm can compare the stored degree with the sequence-tree interval size, then either scan the adjacency list or enumerate the interval and query a deterministic edge dictionary. Its probes and generated candidates equal the chosen minimum up to logarithmic overhead. Claim 4 supplies correctness, while claim 2's remaining accounting is unchanged, giving Õ(m+n√m+H). Each minimum is bounded by the corresponding scanned degree, so H≤A termwise. In claim 3's family, f=v and b=u_i are adjacent, giving forward cost min{r,1}=1 and backward cost min{0,1}=0 per update; hence H=r=O(m).",
      "witness": "On the r-update rescanning family, A=r² but the selective parameter is exactly H=r.",
      "search_method": "Operation-by-operation cost reconstruction, termwise comparison with A, and exact family simulation.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_incremental_toposort_nsqrtm/audit/plain/attempt_6/audit_attempt6_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 6,
      "claim": "The selective parameter H is still not bounded by Õ(n√m): there is a DAG sequence with n=3r+2 and m=4r in which every violating update has q=1 and creates exactly one new reachability pair, but both the forward degree and active forward interval have size at least r, giving H=r².",
      "claim_sha256": "09b467146550974502671baf8c76af42f1501abad481057c9d93121c57a1d6ba",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "In the order v,x₁,…,x_r,u₁,…,u_r,z,w₁,…,w_r with the stated initial edges, before update u_i→v the maintained order is u₁,…,u_(i−1),v,x₁,…,x_r,u_i,… . The balanced sets are {v},{u_i}; u_i already reaches z and all w_j, so only (u_i,v) is fresh. At forward expansion, outdeg(v)=r and (v,u_i] contains r+1 vertices, contributing r. There are r such updates, so H=r², whereas n√m=(3r+2)·2√r=Θ(r^(3/2)).",
      "witness": "The exact ratio H/(n√m)=r²/((3r+2)·2√r)=Θ(√r), which is not polylogarithmically bounded.",
      "search_method": "Exact update-sequence simulation and asymptotic ratio calculation.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_incremental_toposort_nsqrtm/audit/plain/attempt_6/audit_attempt6_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 7,
      "claim": "Padding sharpens the selective-expansion obstruction across every subquadratic density: for integers r≥1 and 0≤s≤r, adjoining a disconnected s-vertex transitive DAG to the preceding sequence gives n=3r+s+2, m=4r+binom(s,2), while every violating update still has q=1, creates one new reachability pair, and contributes total H=r². Consequently H/(n√m)=Θ(r/√(r+s²)). For every fixed a∈[1,2), choosing s=⌈r^(a/2)⌉ gives m=Θ(n^a) and a polynomial gap Θ(n^(1−a/2)); at a=3/2 the gap is Θ(n^(1/4)), whereas at the quadratic or polylogarithmically near-quadratic boundary it is only constant or polylogarithmic.",
      "claim_sha256": "2969e3f31cd6707b0a2c5cfef101de7b87625f54f4773c9a78c36373440a1452",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "The disconnected padding adds exactly s vertices and binom(s,2) order-consistent edges and cannot affect searches or reachability in the original component. Since s≤r, n=Θ(r), m=Θ(r+s²), and H=r², yielding the displayed ratio. For fixed 1≤a<2 and s=⌈r^(a/2)⌉, n=Θ(r), m=Θ(r^a), and the ratio is Θ(r^(1−a/2))=Θ(n^(1−a/2)). Setting r=t⁴,s=t³ gives the exact a=3/2 scaling and n^(1/4) gap. Taking s=Θ(r) gives a constant gap; taking s=r/polylog(r) gives a polylogarithmic gap.",
      "witness": "The integer parameterization r=t⁴,s=t³ has H=t⁸, n=Θ(t⁴), and m=Θ(t⁶), so H/(n√m)=Θ(t)=Θ(n^(1/4)).",
      "search_method": "Exact edge/vertex counting, component-separation reasoning, and integer parameter checks.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_incremental_toposort_nsqrtm/audit/plain/attempt_6/audit_attempt6_checker.py"
    }
  ],
  "confirmed_refutations": [],
  "target_verdict": "VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS",
  "claimed_resolution_verdict": "ACCURATE",
  "target_evidence": "The draft proves valid regime comparisons, a balanced-cut compatible-search framework with conditional Õ(m+n√m+A) and Õ(m+n√m+H) bounds, and explicit families showing why its scan parameters can exceed the target. It does not bound A or H by Õ(n√m) in general and expressly supplies no different unconditional combinatorial algorithm. Thus it makes material correct progress but does not prove the entire requested target. Its stated PARTIAL resolution is accurate.",
  "overall": "VERIFIED",
  "checks_performed": [
    "Read only /evidence/source.json and /evidence/parent.json among evidence inputs; used no web, retrieval database, receipt, other arm, prior-run material, or other solution.",
    "Verified /evidence/source.json SHA-256 as 00067fea545c0d322d41d05de2ddbbdcbb729e74c154d7cbe30d337b0bf80969.",
    "Verified /evidence/parent.json SHA-256 as 508aa9f77a685486000c0b4f9c59054371d98c734d4e542c026043683a951220.",
    "Recomputed all eight claim-string SHA-256 bindings; every binding matched the supplied value.",
    "Persisted and ran /work/audit_attempt6_checker.py (SHA-256 c7551ab089d4d77ad6dc090dc08475f9d8d89ffd24adb8ebaea11248831fe863).",
    "Exhaustively checked 33,866 fixed-order DAGs and 251,085 candidate violating insertions through six vertices, including cycle detection, full-versus-pruned search agreement, balanced cuts, stable reorders, and fresh B×F pairs.",
    "Checked the obstruction constructions exactly for every 1≤r≤40 and all 0≤s≤r, along with exact integer regime inequalities and the r=t⁴,s=t³ crossover parameterization."
